items.title: AAIF Reading Group: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting
items.summary: Can forgetting help AI agents discover better solutions? And why do agents sometimes stop making progress, even when given more time, compute, and opportunities to experiment? Join the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) community for an informal reading group exploring the paper “Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting.” Paper: https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2610.20563 Event page: https://home.mlops.community/public/events/aaif-reading-group-scaling-discovery-requires-forgetting-pg1zmi4qzx In this session, Sparsh Jain walks us through the paper's approach to improving long-running discovery and research tasks by periodically resetting agent sessions and search history while preserving the best candidate discovered so far. We'll explore how agents can become stuck in repetitive patterns, why simply adding more parallel agents or compute may not be enough, and how strategically forgetting previous attempts can help renew exploration and improve results. This is not just about the paper's proposed approach. It's a community conversation about agent memory, context management, autonomous research, and the challenges of scaling agent systems in practice. Following the presentation, Arthur Coleman leads an open discussion, bringing in questions, practical experiences, and different perspectives from the community. We'll explore: Why AI agents plateau during long-running discovery and research tasks How periodically resetting agent context can improve exploration and results The role of parallel agents and collaboration in scaling discovery What agents should remember, what they should forget, and when they should reset The importance of memory reduction, evaluation, and context management Practical challenges and limitations of applying this approach to real-world agent systems If you've read the paper already, come ready to share your perspective. If you haven't, you're still welcome – we'll work through the ideas together. Come curious. Bring questions. Let's explore whether sometimes, forgetting is exactly what makes AI agents better. About the Agentic AI Foundation The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) is the open, neutral home for the agentic AI ecosystem, bringing together developers, researchers, companies, and communities to build open standards and infrastructure for interoperable AI agents. Website: https://aaif.io/ AAIF Events: https://aaif.io/events AAIF Community: https://aaif.live/ LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/agentic-ai-foundation/

items.title: Can AI stop exam paper leaks in India? Inside the Bharat EduAI Stack
